h0_summary.rationale: Soethoudt et al. 2017 (Nat Commun; DOI 10.1038/ncomms13958) provides a unified hCB2 CHO panel with explicit CP55940 normalization in both cAMP (Suppl. Table 4) and GTPgammaS (Suppl. Table 3). Hanus 1999 adds independent HU-308 cAMP on hCB2 CHO. Ordinal tiers are assay-dependent: cAMP lacks a clean PARTIAL tier; GTPgammaS supports TOTAL / PARTIAL / INVERSE separation among five compounds. HU-433 lacks comparable hCB2 Gi row with CP55940 reference in recovered primaries.

h0_entries_table.reported_notes: Soethoudt 2017 Suppl. Table 4: Emax 98±1% vs 10 µM CP55940 (self-reference normalization). CHO hCB2 Nano-TRF cAMP. Consistent full agonist across cAMP and GTPgammaS in same study.
Soethoudt 2017 Suppl. Table 3: Emax 95±4% vs 10 µM CP55940. Narrative: potent full agonist at hCB2R in GTPgammaS assay.
Soethoudt 2017 Suppl. Table 4: cAMP Emax 98±1% (full vs CP55940). Same study Suppl. Table 3: GTPgammaS Emax 49±7% (partial). Assay-dependent efficacy — not a single universal Gi class.
Soethoudt 2017 Suppl. Table 3: Emax 49±7% vs CP55940; narrative labels WIN55212-2 as partial agonist in GTPgammaS at hCB2. cAMP row in same study shows 98±1% — cross-assay discordance documented.
Soethoudt 2017 Suppl. Table 4: cAMP Emax 98±1% vs CP55940 (full). Suppl. Table 3 GTPgammaS: Emax 61±15% (partial). Highly CB2-selective in both assays; efficacy tier assay-dependent.
Soethoudt 2017 Suppl. Table 3: Emax 61±15% vs CP55940 at hCB2. mCB2 full agonist (103±7%) in same table — species/context dependence noted.

Soethoudt 2017 Suppl. Table 4: Emax 98±1% vs CP55940. Independent primary Hanus 1999 (PNAS; 10.1073/pnas.96.25.14228): forskolin-stimulated cAMP inhibition EC50 5.57 nM, Emax 108.6±8.4% (n=5) on hCB2 CHO — CP=100 normalization not atomic in Hanus Results.

Hanuš 1999 direct primary (10.1073/pnas.96.25.14228): hCB2 CHO stable transfection, forskolin cAMP inhibition Emax 108.6±8.4% (n=5). Reference agonist for percent normalization not explicitly stated as CP55940 in Results — separate row from Soethoudt cross-study row.
Soethoudt 2017 Suppl. Table 3: Emax 97±12% vs CP55940; narrative: CP55940 and HU308 behaved as potent full agonists at hCB2R in GTPgammaS.

HU-308 enantiomer / paired mechanistic probe (Hanus 2015 PNAS 10.1073/pnas.1503395112; patent US20110269842A1). Binding Ki 12.2 nM vs HU-308 22.7 nM; authors report higher biological potency despite lower CP55940 displacement and GTPgammaS differences — proposed distinct binding conformations. No recovered hCB2 cAMP/GTPgammaS row with explicit CP55940 Emax% in project primaries — do not invent numbers or force class identical to HU-308.

Not in Soethoudt unified hCB2 panel. Soethoudt reports Delta9-THC (not THCV) GTPgammaS hCB2 Emax 21±3% — do not substitute for THCV. Pertwee 2008 (10.1038/sj.bjp.0707442) describes diverse CB2 pharmacology of plant cannabinoids including THCV but without a single comparable hCB2 Gi Emax% row normalized to CP55940 in recovered tables. Cross-system reviews note partial/CB1-antagonist context — incompatible for forced ordinal intermediate placement.

Soethoudt 2017 Suppl. Table 4: Emax -151±10% vs CP55940 EC80 background (negative = inverse agonism). Historical literature also classifies SR144528 as CB2 antagonist / inverse agonist in constitutively active hCB2 systems — both descriptors noted.
Soethoudt 2017 Suppl. Table 3: Emax -29±2% vs CP55940 (negative values = inverse agonism per table footnote). Antagonist label retained in historical CB2 literature.

Soethoudt 2017 Suppl. Table 4: Emax -152±13% in CP55940 EC80 cAMP assay (inverse-like numeric sign). Literature and in vivo contexts show CB2 antagonist, neutral antagonist, or inverse agonist behavior depending on constitutive receptor activity and species (cf. Hanus 2017 note on AM-630 vs selective inverse agonists). Do NOT auto-assign universal INVERSE — protocol and basal activity dependent.
Soethoudt 2017 Suppl. Table 3: Emax -22±2% at hCB2 vs CP55940. CB1 row near neutral (-1±1%). Functional sign assay- and receptor-state dependent — PROTEAN_OR_SYSTEM_DEPENDENT per PI governance.

coordinate.interpretation: Receptor-state fingerprint distance to active centroid (6PT0+6KPF). Ligand projection = distance of multistate-docking preferred receptor state to that centroid — NOT ligand pose fingerprint, NOT Vina score as Gi Emax.

projection_method.name: multistate_preferred_state_to_active_centroid
honest_limitations: Vina score is NOT used as functional Emax proxy
Ligands without multistate docking lack defined projection
Identical receptor-state distance can mask pose/orientation differences (HU-308/HU-433)

functional_dissociation_literature.note: Authors (Hanus 2015) report HU-433 higher biological potency despite lower CP55940 displacement and GTPgammaS differences — distinct binding conformations proposed. Do not collapse into one functional class.

receptor_state_projection.interpretation: Identical receptor-state centroid distance for both ligands (pose selects same PDB state), yet pose-conditioned microswitch contacts differ (Trp258 5.15 vs 6.47 Å) and literature reports affinity vs Gi efficacy dissociation. Supports orientation/conformation mechanism over simple 'distance = Emax' ordinal.
